# Garden share: decomposition proposal

This is the vision decomposer's proposal for `plans/vision/garden-share.md`. **No functional plan stubs exist
yet.** The library that creates them (`src/lib/vision-decomposer.js`) is not in this project root, so the stubs
were not created. See "Steps for the session" at the end. This proposal waits for the owner's OK at the
decomposition checkpoint. It has not been handed to the Product Owner.

## Ancestry read

- Vision: `plans/vision/garden-share.md`. It has `type: vision` and `status: ready`.
- Canvas: none. `plans/canvas/garden-share.md` does not exist, because the only file under `plans/` is the vision.
  So the goals come from the vision alone.
- Existing stubs or plans: none, because `plans/functional/` does not exist.

## Impact map

| # | Goal (business outcome) | Actor | Impact (behaviour change) | Success metric | Vision criterion |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| G1 | Garden owners publish unused garden space as a plot offer in under five minutes | Garden owner in the town with space they do not use | Offers the space openly to growers instead of relying on word of mouth | Median time from opening "Offer a plot" to the offer being live is under 5 minutes, measured from recorded timestamps | 1 |
| G2 | Growers on the waiting list find and request a plot within one kilometre in under five minutes | Person on the town's allotment waiting list who wants to grow vegetables | Finds a nearby plot on offer and asks for it, instead of waiting three years | Median time from starting a search to a sent request is under 5 minutes, for searches with at least one plot within 1 km | 2 |

The requesting grower receives the outcome. | The owner accepts or declines promptly. An accepted owner and grower get each other's details and meet. | At least 50 accepted requests ("shared plots") within six months of launch, counted from recorded accept events | 3 |

## Story map

`[MVP]` marks the Walking Skeleton: the thinnest path that works end to end through all three goals. It is a
technical identification, not a schedule. The owner chooses what is built and when.

Points: 1 point is about half a day, and 3 points is about 3 days, which is the upper limit for a small story.

### G1: Offer a plot

Activities (backbone): 1.1 Describe and publish the plot, then 1.2 Keep the offer up to date.

#### Activity 1.1: Describe and publish the plot

- [ ] **S1.1.1 [MVP]** As a garden owner, I want to enter my address, the plot's size and the times growers may
  come, and publish it with only my email address, so that growers can find my plot after less than five minutes of my time. *(3 pts, no dependencies)*
  - Acceptance: an address inside the town is geocoded and stored with coordinates. An address outside the town is
    rejected with "Garden share covers <town> only".
  - Acceptance: size is required, in m², as a whole number from 1 to 1000. Access times are one or more weekday
    plus time windows (for example Saturday 09:00–12:00), and at least one is required.
  - Acceptance: "Publish" asks for an email address and sends a one-time sign-in link that is valid for 30 minutes.
    Clicking it creates the owner account and puts the offer live. An expired link offers "Send a new link".
  - Acceptance: the timestamps "offer form opened" and "offer live" are recorded for each offer.
- [ ] **S1.1.2** As a garden owner, I want to move the map pin to where the plot actually is, so that the distance
  growers see is correct when the plot is far from the house entrance. *(1–2 pts, depends on S1.1.1)*
  - Acceptance: after geocoding, a map shows a draggable pin. The pin cannot be dropped outside the town boundary.
    The stored coordinates are the pin's coordinates.
- [ ] **S1.1.3** As a garden owner, I want to add a short description and up to three photos (sun, soil, water
  tap), so that growers can judge the plot before they ask for it. *(2 pts, depends on S1.1.1)*
  - Acceptance: the description is at most 500 characters. Photos are JPEG or PNG, at most 5 MB each, and at most
    3. Publishing works with neither.

#### Activity 1.2: Keep the offer up to date

- [ ] **S1.2.1 [MVP]** As a garden owner, I want to sign in again with an emailed link and withdraw my offer, so
  that I stop receiving requests once the space is gone. *(2 pts, depends on S1.1.1)*
  - Acceptance: "Sign in" with an email address sends a one-time link that is valid for 30 minutes. After sign-in,
    "My offer" shows the offer.
  - Acceptance: "Withdraw" asks for confirmation. Afterwards the public page of the offer shows "This plot is no
    longer offered", and the offer is not in the set of live offers that search reads.
- [ ] **S1.2.2** As a garden owner, I want to change the size, access times, description or photos of my live
  offer, so that growers always see what is really available. *(2 pts, depends on S1.2.1)*
  - Acceptance: saved changes appear on the public page on the next page load. A changed address runs geocoding
    and the town check again.

### G2: Find and request a plot

Activities (backbone): 2.1 Search near me, then 2.2 Choose and request a plot.

#### Activity 2.1: Search near me

- [ ] **S2.1.1 [MVP]** As a grower, I want to enter my address and see every live plot within one kilometre,
  nearest first, so that I only look at plots I can reach. *(2–3 pts, depends on S1.1.1)*
  - Acceptance: searching needs no account. Given live plots 0.4 km and 1.6 km from the address entered, only the
    0.4 km plot is listed.
  - Acceptance: each result shows the distance to 0.1 km, the size, the access times and the neighbourhood. The
    street address and the exact coordinates are never in the page or in its data response. Distance is computed
    on the server from the exact coordinates.
  - Acceptance: withdrawn and shared plots are not listed. A "search started" timestamp is recorded for each
    search session.
- [ ] **S2.1.2** As a grower, I want to see the results on a map around my address, so that I can judge the
  route. *(2 pts, depends on S2.1.1)*
  - Acceptance: the map is centred on the address entered and shows a 1 km circle. Each plot is shown at a rounded
    position (a grid of about 200 m), never its exact one. Clicking a plot shows its size and distance and a link
    to the plot.
- [ ] **S2.1.3** As a grower, I want to filter the results by minimum size and by access day, so that I only see
  plots that fit my plans. *(1–2 pts, depends on S2.1.1)*
  - Acceptance: with the filter "at least 20 m², Saturday", a 15 m² plot and a plot with only weekday windows are
    hidden. Clearing the filter shows them again.
- [ ] **S2.1.4** As a grower, I want to leave my email address when there is no plot within one kilometre and be
  emailed when one is offered, so that I do not have to keep checking. *(2–3 pts, depends on S2.1.1 and S1.1.1)*
  - Acceptance: an empty result shows "No plots within 1 km right now" and an email field. When an offer goes live
    within 1 km of the saved address, exactly one email is sent with a link to it. Every email has a one-click
    unsubscribe link.

#### Activity 2.2: Choose and request a plot

- [ ] **S2.2.1 [MVP]** As a grower, I want to open a plot and send its owner a request with a short message, so
  that the owner knows who I am and why I want it. *(3 pts, depends on S1.1.1)*
  - Acceptance: the plot page shows the size, the access times, any description and photos, the distance and the
    neighbourhood. It never shows the street address.
  - Acceptance: the request form asks for a name, a message of at most 500 characters and an email address. A
    first-time grower confirms by a one-time emailed link, which uses the same mechanism as S1.1.1. After
    confirmation the request is stored as "pending" and the grower sees "Request sent".
  - Acceptance: a second pending request from the same grower for the same plot is refused with "You already asked
    for this plot". A "request sent" timestamp is recorded and linked to the search session.
- [ ] **S2.2.2** As a grower, I want to state that I am on the town's allotment waiting list and since which year,
  so that owners can give priority to growers from the waiting list. *(1 pt, depends on S2.2.1)*
  - Acceptance: the request form has an "I am on the allotment waiting list" checkbox and an optional year from
    2000 to the current year. Both are stored on the request. The grower declares this; nobody verifies it.
- [ ] **S2.2.3** As a grower, I want to see all my requests with their status and withdraw a pending one, so that
  I know where I stand. *(2 pts, depends on S2.2.1)*
  - Acceptance: after sign-in by an emailed link, "My requests" lists each request with its plot, date and status
    (pending, accepted, declined, no longer available, expired or withdrawn). "Withdraw" on a pending request sets
    it to withdrawn, and it no longer counts as pending for the owner.

### G3: Answer plot requests

Activities (backbone): 3.1 Review and answer requests, then 3.2 Settle the plot after a decision.

#### Activity 3.1: Review and answer requests

- [ ] **S3.1.1 [MVP]** As a garden owner, I want to be emailed about a new request and accept it on the request's
  page, so that the grower and I can meet and start. *(3 pts, depends on S2.2.1)*
  - Acceptance: within one minute of a request becoming pending, the owner receives an email with the grower's
    name, the message, any other fields stored on the request, and a one-time link that signs the owner in to the
    request page.
  - Acceptance: "Accept" sets the status to accepted and records an accept timestamp. It marks the offer as shared,
    so that the offer leaves the set of live offers.
  - Acceptance: on acceptance the grower is emailed the owner's street address, access times and email address,
    and the owner's request page shows the grower's email address. Before acceptance, neither party's address or
    email is in any page or data response that the other party can open.
- [ ] **S3.1.2 [MVP]** As a garden owner, I want to decline a request with an optional reason, so that the grower
  is free to look elsewhere. *(1 pt, depends on S3.1.1)*
  - Acceptance: "Decline", with an optional reason of at most 300 characters, sets the status to declined. The
    grower is emailed the outcome and the reason if one was given. The email does not contain the owner's address
    or email.
- [ ] **S3.1.3** As a garden owner, I want one page that lists all requests for my plot, oldest first, so that I
  can compare growers before I answer. *(2 pts, depends on S3.1.1 and S1.2.1)*
  - Acceptance: a signed-in owner sees the pending requests with name, date, waiting-list statement and the first
    100 characters of the message. Each one opens its request page. Only the owner of the plot can open the list.
    Any other signed-in user gets "not found".
- [ ] **S3.1.4** As a grower whose request has not been answered, I want the owner to be reminded after 7 days and
  the request to be closed after 14 days, so that I am not left waiting with no end. *(2 pts, depends on S3.1.1)*
  - Acceptance: on day 7 of a pending request, the owner receives one reminder email with a link to the request
    page. On day 14 the status becomes expired and the grower is emailed. An expired request cannot be accepted.

#### Activity 3.2: Settle the plot after a decision

- [ ] **S3.2.1 [MVP]** As a grower whose request is still pending when the owner accepts someone else or withdraws
  the offer, I want to be told that the plot is no longer available, so that I do not wait for an answer that
  will never come. *(1–2 pts, depends on S3.1.1 and S1.2.1)*
  - Acceptance: accepting another request, or withdrawing the offer (S1.2.1), sets every other pending request for
    that plot to "no longer available". Each of those growers is emailed exactly once.
- [ ] **S3.2.2** As a garden owner or grower in a share, I want to end the share and let the owner offer the plot
  again in one step, so that the space does not sit unused after a season. *(2 pts, depends on S3.1.1)*
  - Acceptance: either party can click "End share". The share then has status ended and the other party is
    emailed. The owner then sees "Offer this plot again", which puts the same offer live with its previous details.
- [ ] **S3.2.3** As the service operator, I want to see how many plots have been shared since launch, per month,
  so that I can tell whether we are on course for 50 in six months. *(1–2 pts, depends on S3.1.1)*
  - Acceptance: an operator-only page shows the accepted requests per calendar month and the total since the launch
    date. The numbers equal a count of the recorded accept events. People who are not operators get "not found".

```
S1.1.1 ─┬─ S1.1.2
        ├─ S1.1.3
        ├─ S1.2.1 ── S1.2.2
```

- Cycles: none. A depth-first walk from every node never returns to its start.
- Direct dependencies per story: 2 at most (S2.1.4, S3.1.3 and S3.2.1 have 2).
- Stub-level chain: answer plot requests, then find and request a plot, then offer a plot. That is depth 3, which
  is within the limit. The "Answer plot requests" stub depends directly on both other stubs (2 direct dependencies,
  within the limit).
- **Story-level chain depth: 4 for six G3 stories.** These are S3.1.2, S3.1.3, S3.1.4, S3.2.1, S3.2.2 and S3.2.3,
  each through S3.1.1, then S2.2.1, then S1.1.1. That is one level over the limit of 3. See decision D15.
- Cross-goal dependencies follow the matching flow, where an offer must exist before a request, and a request
  before an answer. They do not come from shared code that makes the goals overlap.

Topological order within each stub:
- Offer a plot: S1.1.1, then S1.1.2, S1.1.3 and S1.2.1, then S1.2.2.
- Find and request a plot: S2.1.1 and S2.2.1, which need S1.1.1, then S2.1.2, S2.1.3, S2.1.4, S2.2.2 and S2.2.3.

  (which also needs S1.2.1), S3.2.2 and S3.2.3.

Walking Skeleton path: S1.1.1, S1.2.1, S2.1.1, S2.2.1, S3.1.1, S3.1.2 and S3.2.1. A plot is offered, found within
1 km and requested, then accepted or declined, contact details are exchanged, and the other requesters are told.

## Decisions Taken Under Ambiguity (awaiting owner review)

- **D1. No canvas.** The goals come from the vision only.
- **D2. Three goals, one for each success criterion, and one stub for each goal.** The actor and impact pairs
  differ for each criterion. Merging all three into one stub would give 19 stories, which is over the cap of 15
  stories per stub. *Alternative:* one cross-goal "Walking Skeleton" stub with the 7 MVP stories, plus stubs for
  the remaining stories.
- **D3. Sign-in by an emailed one-time link, with no passwords, for owners and growers.** It keeps the owner's flow
  under 5 minutes. *Alternative:* accounts with passwords.
- **D4. The five-minute clock for owners includes the round trip of the email link.** The offer goes live when
  the owner clicks the link. Both metrics are medians computed from recorded timestamps. *Alternatives:* the offer
  goes live before the email is confirmed, or the target is "every owner in a usability test" instead of a median.
- **D5. Waiting-list membership is declared by the grower and not verified.** The vision gives no information
  about the town's waiting-list register. *Alternative:* verification against the register, which would need a
  time-boxed investigation first.
- **D6. An owner's street address and exact position are never shown before acceptance.** Search shows the
  distance and neighbourhood, and the map shows a position rounded to about 200 m. Both parties' contact details
  are revealed on acceptance.
- **D7. One plot goes to one grower.** Accepting a request closes the other pending requests for that plot.
  *Alternative:* an owner shares one garden among several growers, which would need a "number of places" field.
- **D8. Reminder after 7 days, expiry after 14 days.** I chose both numbers.
- **D9. "Plot shared" means a request was accepted, counted at the accept event.** *Alternative:* both parties
  confirm after the first visit.
- **D10. "Within one kilometre" is straight-line distance**, not a walking route.
- **D11. One town, enforced by a boundary check.** The vision does not name the town, so the geocoding service and
  the map data are still open (this belongs in the implementation plan).
- **D12. Delivered as a responsive website.** The vision excludes a mobile app, so phones use the browser.
- **D13. Searching needs no account. Only sending a request needs a confirmed email address.**
- **D14. A "service operator" actor was added for the count of shared plots (S3.2.3).** The vision does not say
  who runs the service.
- **D15. A story-level chain of depth 4 is accepted for six G3 stories.** The order offer, then request, then
  answer, then what follows the answer is how the matching works. Reaching depth 3 would require merging an
  answer-related story into S3.1.1, which is already at 3 points, and that story would then fail Small. The
  stub-level chain stays at depth 3.
- **D16. The concrete limits in the acceptance criteria are my proposals.** They are: 1 to 1000 m², 500 characters,
  3 photos of 5 MB, a 30-minute link, a 200 m rounding grid and a reason of 300 characters.
- **D17. The interactive questions were not asked, because this work runs in the background.** The goals follow
  D2. The delivery strategy (Walking Skeleton first, goal by goal, or actor by actor) is **not chosen**. That
  choice belongs to the owner.
- **D18. The library is absent, so no stubs were created.** `src/lib/vision-decomposer.js` is not in this project
  root. The proposal is in this new file under `plans/decomposition/`, because I know of no pipeline convention for
  it. The slug format that `dependsOn` expects (the full stub slug or only the goal slug) is not verified.
